    a `resource` prerequisite naming that need and, only when the worker has no unavailable
    reading of that instance in force, a reading `available: false` (`valid_for` 1 hour) of it
    — a reading already in force (for `roadmap-pr`, the one its worker posts with the
    provider's reset, `BATON_ROADMAP_PR_COURSE` R-BTN-42) is kept, and its `until` never
    shortened; and R-BTN-76's per-worker answer gives today's effect — the leg is
    lowered for that worker's account for an hour, and another account continues. With none
    or several — Baton cannot tell which account ran out — the end is recorded `blocked`
    with no reading; it **counts toward `max_blocked`** unless the worker has an unavailable
    reading in force for an instance serving the leg's needs (for `roadmap-pr`, the R-BTN-42
    reading of the account it billed, which also lowers the leg for it), so no course escapes
    the bound. Every legacy end counts toward the worker's **Needs you** threshold.
  - **A blocked edge, drawn as one.** Wherever Baton draws a course — the dashboard's
    **Courses** view, a ticket's path, `baton leg why` — every leg is an edge between stations
    with a state: `ready`; `running` (a claim holds it); `blocked`, with the kind of each unmet
    prerequisite, its `since` and `until`, and whether it was found before a start or during a
    run (`ticket_blocks.found`, `before-start` or `during-run`: a `resource` row is
    `during-run` while its need carries a `blocked` end's `found_at` stamp, whether the need was
    posted or `end`-sourced and whoever wrote the row; a `capability`, `ticket` or `decision`
    row a `blocked` end causes is `during-run`; every other row, including one that predates
    the claim, is `before-start`); `backing-off` (a `retry` block); or `not-queued`. A
    blocked edge is never drawn as a station, and each state is shown by colour **and** a text
    label (§14 forbids colour alone). The view is Baton's, from the blocks index and
    `leg_needs`; a course adds no node for it.

### 2m.6d The CLI as a command tree, and a leg's log

*(Owner, 2026-10-17: "I would like the Baton CLI to have a Git-like command, subcommand
hierarchy where, for example, all the commands that pertain to a given leg of a ticket would
have the prefix baton leg … baton leg log would give you the logs produced by the leg of a
given ticket." Asked how a finished leg's log is kept, the owner chose to save each leg run's
output now, and to rename the old commands outright, with no aliases.)*

- **R-BTN-127 (the CLI is a tree of nouns and verbs).** *(Amended 2026-10-17 by §2m: the tree below is generated from the registry's command table, and each command's **Signs as** is its actions' `callers`, in order — R-BTN-129.)* *(Amends R-BTN-58, R-BTN-72, R-BTN-74,
  R-BTN-80, R-BTN-84, R-BTN-106, R-BTN-117, §2d, §3a, §6.13 and every command this spec
  names.)* Every command is `baton <noun> <verb> [<arguments>] [<flags>]`, as `git remote add`
  is; the only top-level verbs are `help` and `version`. Each command signs as one key role
  (R-BTN-57: one role per key) — the **Signs as** column — with the key `-i <file>` names,
  else the one the CLI's configuration maps to that role (`~/.config/baton/keys.json`:
  `{admin, owner: {<repository>: <file>}, courier, worker, sync: {<repository>: <file>},
  mirror: {<repository>: <file>}}`, *2026-10-18, R-BTN-137:* one such object per origin, `{<origin>: {…}}`); a command with no key for its role exits 2 naming the
  role. Where a row names two roles, the CLI tries the first it has a key for, in the order
  written. `repo sync` and `repo mirror` sign, in order, with a CI identity token the
  environment provides (GitHub Actions OIDC, or a GitLab `id_tokens` JWT in
  `BATON_CI_TOKEN`; R-BTN-93), the repository's sync or mirror key, or the worker's machine
  key where R-BTN-102 lets a machine key sync.

  | Command | Route | Signs as | Was |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `leg why <ticket> [<leg>]` | `GET …/tickets/{ticket}/prerequisites` (R-BTN-120) | owner, or worker granted on the repository | `baton why` |
  | `leg log <ticket> [<leg>] [--run <n>] [-f] [--transcripts] [--json]` | `GET …/tickets/{ticket}/legs/{leg}/runs`, git, `GET /v1/stream` (R-BTN-128) | owner, or administrator | — |
  | `leg runs <ticket> [<leg>]` | `GET …/tickets/{ticket}/legs/{leg}/runs` | owner, or administrator | — |
  | `leg replay <ticket> <leg> [--run <n>] [--against <sha>]` | as R-BTN-84 | as R-BTN-84 | `baton replay` |
  | `leg stop <ticket>` (**Stop leg**, R-BTN-119) | `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/tickets/{ticket}/release` *(new)*, `{reason: 'requested', confirm: true}` | owner | — |
  | `status`, `output`, `done`, `suspend`, `release`, `next`, `yield` (inside a leg) | the local channel (R-BTN-106) | — (the runner signs) | unchanged |
  | `ticket blocked [<ticket>] [--on <kind>:<ref>]` | the blocks routes (R-BTN-75) | owner, or worker granted on the repository | `baton blocked` |
  | `ticket history <ticket>` | `GET …/tickets/{ticket}/history` (§11) | owner, or worker granted on the repository | — |
  | `course test <root> <course> [--base <ref>] [--board <file>]` | none: a local Baton (§2d) | — | `baton test-course` |
  | `repo init [--course create-pr\|review-pr\|bug-report\|draft-ticket\|decision\|branch\|epic] [--override <leg>]… [--forge …] [--eject tickets\|stations]` | none: writes files | — | `baton init` |
  | `repo sync [--if-wanted] [--defaults-only]`, `repo mirror [--if-wanted]` | `/v1/sync/*` (§7.1, R-BTN-93) | a CI identity token, sync (or mirror), or worker (R-BTN-102) |
  | `repo spool <repository>` | none: touches the spool file the sync account watches (R-BTN-105) | — (it runs as the pusher, who never reads the sync key) | `baton sync`, `baton mirror`, `baton spool` |
  | `runner start [--legs …] [--max-legs <n>] [--until <t>] [--attached] [--sessions <provider>] [--course <id>]` | `/v1/runner/*` (§6.13) | worker | `baton run` |
  | `runner register --token <t> --name <name> [--key ssh\|api]` | as R-BTN-117 | the token | `baton register` |
  | `decision list [--all]` | `/v1/courier/*` (the CLI courier, R-BTN-80) | courier | `baton inbox` |
  | `server start --db <file> --admin-keys …` | none: starts the local host (§3a) | — | `baton start` |
  | `admin …`, `owner …` | as R-BTN-57 and R-BTN-58 list them | administrator, owner | — |

  - **A leg is named by its ticket.** `<ticket>` is a qualified id, or a local id unique in the
    signing key's repositories; an id that matches in several exits 2, listing the qualified
    matches. `<leg>` defaults to the ticket's running leg, else its queued leg, else its most
    recent leg; `--run <n>` picks one run of the leg (§2e), default the latest.
  - **Inside a leg.** The channel verbs act on the leg whose socket `IR_BATON_SOCKET` names
    (R-BTN-106) and take no ticket; outside a leg's session they exit 2 with "not inside a
    leg". The other verbs work anywhere.
  - **No aliases.** An old name exits 2 with one line naming its replacement (`baton why`
    → "renamed: baton leg why"), and does nothing else. The spec's rules use the new names;
    its Decisions and Review record keep the names current when each was written. The docs
    repository's callers (its skills, workflows and `BATON_DOCS_DEPLOYMENT`) and the open
    tickets change in the same release (B-23).
  - **Help is part of the tree.** `baton help [<noun> [<verb>]]`, `baton <noun> --help` and
    an unknown verb print that level's commands; an unknown word suggests the nearest name.
    Every command that reads a route takes `--json` and prints the route's JSON as is;
    `leg log --json` prints the run's frames as JSON lines.

- **R-BTN-128 (a leg run's output is saved to git, and `baton leg log` reads it).** *(Amended 2026-10-18 by §10.7: the masked set gains the runner's own credentials, credential values, Baton tokens and private-key blocks; a pointer carries its commit and digest — R-BTN-144.)* *(Amends
  R-BTN-20, R-BTN-33, R-BTN-58, R-BTN-66, R-BTN-118, §6.8, §10.6, §11 and the reserved note
  after R-BTN-125.)* The runner already reads each leg's output to stream it (R-BTN-118); for a
  repository whose owners opt in, it now also saves it, where the repository keeps
  transcripts, so a finished leg has a log Baton never holds.
  - **Opt-in.** Owners turn it on with `leg_logs: true` (R-BTN-66; default `false`), and only
    with at least one `transcript_repos` entry. The runner learns it from the reply that starts each run: the claim's reply for the first
    leg, the `advance` reply for each leg after it. That reply carries `leg_logs: {repo}` —
    the transcript repository to archive to — only while the setting is on, and the runner
    archives a run only when the reply that started it said so; a change of the setting takes
    effect at the next run started. Baton records what it sent on the run
    (`claim_legs.leg_logs_repo`, null when it sent none) and drops, logging `invalid-pointer`,
    a pointer for a run whose record is null or whose `repo` differs from it, so the opt-in
    does not rest on the runner alone. Saving widens who can read a leg's output from
    Baton-authorized viewers to every reader of the transcript repository, so it is never on
    without the owners' word (threat model P5).
  - **What is saved.** For each leg run in `process` mode, the runner reads the leg
    process's stdout and stderr pipes whether or not anyone is watching, and writes them in
    the stream's frame shape, `{seq, at, stream, text}` as JSON lines, with no rate limit.
    **One sequence.** The runner cuts the masked bytes into frames once, numbering them with
    one `seq` per run, and both sinks carry those frames and numbers unchanged — the archive
    every one, the stream (its scrollback included) those it sends. A frame the stream drops
    keeps its number, so a reader sees the hole. `text` is the masked bytes decoded as UTF-8, each invalid byte becoming
    U+FFFD; a frame holds at most 8 KB of `text` as UTF-8, so frames are cut where the decoded
    text reaches that size, between code points, each invalid byte counting as one. `attached` and `session` runs are not archived: their agent runs in the
    session, not as the runner's child, and the session's transcript is their log (§6.8,
    R-BTN-113). A leg the course marks `"stream": false` is neither streamed nor archived.
  - **Where.** The archive is
    `baton-legs/<repository id>/<local ticket id>/<leg>/<run>-<claim id>.jsonl`, every segment
    in §6.8's path class, in the first of the repository's `transcript_repos`, on that
    repository's default branch. The runner pushes with its own git credentials — the machine's
    access to the transcript repository, as the session archivers push (§6.8). The remote is
    `https://github.com/<owner/name>.git` for a GitHub entry, `<web_base>.git` for a
    `<forge>:<web_base>` entry.
  - **How it is pushed.** One commit per push, appending the frames since the last push to the
    run's own file. The runner pushes at the leg's end, and at least every 5 minutes or 1 MB
    while it runs. A rejected push is fetched, rebased (no other writer touches that file) and
    retried, at most five times over ten minutes. Frames not yet pushed are held up to 8 MB;
    past that the oldest give way to one `gap` frame with their count. A push that still fails
    is reported as a `leg-log-push-failed` activity and never delays or fails the leg's end.
  - **Bounds.** At most 50 MB per run; past it the runner writes one `gap` frame with the count
    and stops archiving that run, still streaming it.
  - **Masking.** The runner masks credentials on the byte stream **before** it cuts frames,
    holding back the longest credential's length less one byte, so a credential split
    across two reads or two frames is still caught; the stream and the archive see the same
    masked bytes. Each exact occurrence becomes `***`. The set masked is closed:
    - the worker secret and the claim's nonce;
    - the runner's Baton API key, if it has one (R-BTN-117), and *(2026-10-18, R-BTN-144)* its
      other Baton credentials: `IR_BATON_KEY`, the file `IR_BATON_KEY_FILE` names, and
      `IR_BATON_TOKEN`;
    - the **value** of the environment variable each declared `credential:<NAME>` capability
      names (R-BTN-121, R-BTN-144), given to the leg or not;
    - the git and forge tokens the runner holds, including the one that pushes the archive;
    - *(2026-10-18, R-BTN-144)* by pattern, in the same held-back window: any `brt_`, `bak_` or
      `bmcp_` token, and any `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` … `-----END … -----` block,
      replaced whole.

    A value shorter than 8 bytes is not masked, and the runner logs that once. Masking
    cannot catch a credential that is encoded or transformed, or a secret the agent read
    from the repository or its environment that is not in the set; the archive's
    confidentiality is the transcript repository's read access.
  - **The pointer.** Each push is reported as `(repo, path, pushed_at, bytes, commit, sha256)` *(2026-10-18, R-BTN-144: the commit the push created and the file's digest)* in `leg_logs`, on
    the runner's next heartbeat or on the claim's `advance` or `end`, whichever comes first.
    Pending pointers persist in the runner's state, so a runner that stops after its last leg
    sends them before it exits. Baton keeps the pointer on the leg run (`leg_logs`, §4) — a
    pointer, never the bytes (R-BTN-33). Baton refuses a row whose path fails §6.8's
    Validation, is not the claim's own prescribed path, names a repo outside the repository's
    `transcript_repos`, or names a claim the reporting worker never held: it is dropped and
    logged `invalid-pointer`, and the heartbeat still succeeds. A row is bound to the claim it
    names and is never re-linked to a later one, unlike R-BTN-20's session reports.
  - **`baton leg log`.** The CLI asks Baton for the leg's runs (`GET …/tickets/{ticket}/legs/
    {leg}/runs`: each run's claim, worker, mode, start and end, session link, log pointers and
    transcript pointers).
    - **A finished run:** it reads the archive from git with the user's own credentials and
      prints it.
    - **A running leg:** it prints what the archive holds and then, with `-f`, follows the live
      stream, printing only frames whose `seq` is greater than the last archived one; a missing
      `seq` prints a `[gap]` line.
    - **`--transcripts`:** it also prints the run's agent transcripts from their pointers.
    - **A `session` or `attached` run:** it prints the session link and the transcript
      pointers.
    - **Nothing to print:** with no archive and no stream it prints the run record and why —
      `leg_logs` off, `stream: false`, no `transcript_repos`, or nothing pushed yet.
    - **A failed git read:** it prints the run record, then "cannot read `<repo>`: `<reason>`",
      and exits 1.
    - **Every path:** the CLI strips terminal escape sequences and every C0 and C1 control
      character except newline and tab from all it prints — archive, scrollback, live frames and
      transcripts — since a leg's output is untrusted text (P8).
  - **Watching from the CLI.** R-BTN-118's viewer side gains `GET /v1/stream?claim=<id>`. It is
    an upgrade signed as an owner request is (R-BTN-58), by an owner key of the claim's
    repository or an administrator key, under the same nonce and time window. It takes no
    `Origin`. R-BTN-118's rules on claims, `stream` and bounds apply. A key revoked while it
    watches has its stream closed, as R-BTN-91 closes a revoked worker's socket.
  - **Asking a predecessor session stays reserved** (§2m.6b's note): with the output saved, it
    remains a course leg's feature, built when a course needs it.

### 2m.6e One registry of actions, whatever the surface

*(Owner, 2026-10-17: "I would like a single registry of actions that an authenticated user can
take, depending on what permissions they are granted. It shouldn't matter if they are invoking
this through Baton's REST API or the CLI or an MCP integration for an agent." Asked three
questions, the owner chose to keep today's roles and scopes, to serve MCP from Baton itself,
and to put every route in the registry, with the MCP surface filtered.)*

- **R-BTN-129 (one registry of actions; every surface is derived from it).** *(Amended 2026-10-18 by §10.7: the overrides route also serves `ticket.unhold`, owner or dashboard only — R-BTN-154.)* *(Amended 2026-10-18 by §3b: the scope `instance` means this tenant, and no action is the operator's — R-BTN-136)* *(Amends §10.1,
  §10.6, §11, §14's Actions, R-BTN-57, R-BTN-58 and R-BTN-127.)*
  - **An action** is one entry in `src/shared/actions.mjs`, Baton's own shared code:
    `{id, summary, callers, effect, input, output, http, ui?, mcp}`.
    - `id` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)+$` — dots and hyphens, never `_` —
      in R-BTN-127's nouns: `leg.why`, `leg.stop`, `ticket.expedite`, `owner.owners.add`,
      `runner.heartbeat`.
    - `callers` lists every principal that may call it, each with its scope. Order matters:
      the CLI tries them in this order.
      - The principals: `administrator`, `dashboard` (a dashboard session, which acts as the
        administrator), `owner`, `worker`, `courier`, `probe`, `check-runner`, `sync`, `mirror`,
        `mcp` (R-BTN-130), `token` (a registration token, R-BTN-117), `webhook` (the GitHub App's
        signature), `forge` (a forge verifier, R-BTN-95), and `public` (no credential:
        `POST /v1/login`, `GET /v1/keys/signing`).
      - The scopes: `instance`, `repository` (the route's repository is one the key owns or is
        granted on), `claim-holder` (the key holds the claim's lease), `own` (its own
        credential or notices), `instances` (a probe's allowed instances, R-BTN-53), and `asks`
        (a courier's labels, R-BTN-80).
    - `effect` is `read`, `write` or `destructive`.
    - `input` and `output` are schemas in the shared validator's subset (R-BTN-108).
    - `http` is the route: `{method, path, upgrade?: 'websocket', match?}`. A WebSocket upgrade
      (`/v1/runner/push`, `/v1/runner/stream`, `/v1/ui/stream`, `/v1/stream`) is an action,
      authorized at the upgrade. `match` names a body field's value, for a route that serves
      more than one action: `POST …/overrides/{ticket}` is `ticket.expedite`, `ticket.hold`
      (`hold: true`), `ticket.unhold` (`hold: false`) and `ticket.cancel`, told apart by which
      field is set and, for `hold`, its value *(2026-10-18, R-BTN-154)*, and a body that matches no action
      or several is `invalid-params`.
    - `ui` is the dashboard control (§14).
    - `mcp` is whether R-BTN-130 may expose the action.
  - **Destructive actions, by id:**
    - `ticket.cancel`, `leg.stop`, `claim.force-reap`;
    - `owner.owners.remove`, `owner.grant.revoke`, `owner.courier.revoke`,
      `owner.check-runner.revoke`, `owner.token.revoke`, `owner.mcp-key.revoke`;
    - `admin.key.revoke`, `admin.repo.retire`;
    - *(2026-10-18, §10.7)* `admin.sessions.revoke`.

    Each of these routes takes `confirm: true` in its body, or is refused `confirm-required`.
    The CLI asks for it, or takes `--yes`; the dashboard's confirmation dialogs send it.
  - **The CLI's commands** are a second table in the same file: each command names the
    action ids it calls (`leg log` calls `leg.runs`, `leg.stream` and reads git), or `local`
    for one that calls none (`course test`, `repo init`, `repo spool`, `server start`, the
    channel verbs, `help`). R-BTN-127's tree and every `--help` are generated from it, and a
    command's **Signs as** is its actions' `callers`, in order.
  - **One check.** The front resolves the request's credential to a principal and a target,
    then calls `authorize(principal, action, target)` in core. It is one function, whichever
    surface the call came from, and no route, command, dashboard control or MCP tool checks
    permissions itself.
    - Under `/v1`, a request that matches no entry is answered `404` `not-found`; the
      dashboard's static assets are not actions.
    - A dashboard session authorizes as `dashboard`. An administrator's actions, and an owner
      action whose `callers` list `dashboard`, are open to it on every repository (§14).
  - **The surfaces are generated from it.**
    - The router's table comes from `http`.
    - The CLI tree comes from the command table.
    - The MCP tool list comes from `mcp`.

    §11's rows document the registry. `npm run check:actions` fails when:
    - a route, a command or a §11 row has no entry;
    - an entry has neither a route nor a command;
    - an id breaks the grammar;
    - an `mcp: true` entry falls outside R-BTN-130's allowlist.
  - **What can I do.** `GET /v1/actions` answers the caller's own entries: those its principal
    and scopes allow, each with its `input` schema. `baton help` with a key reads it, and so
    does MCP's `tools/list`. A caller is never shown an action it cannot take.

- **R-BTN-130 (Baton serves MCP).** *(Amended 2026-10-18 by §10.7: MCP's writes are `ticket.hold` (add only) and `leg.stop` (owner, 2026-10-18) — R-BTN-154.)* *(Amends §10.1, §11, R-BTN-57, R-BTN-58, R-BTN-66 and
  R-BTN-117.)*
  - **What MCP may reach is a closed list.** `mcp: true` is allowed only on:
    - an action whose `effect` is `read`, whose `callers` include `owner`, and which is no
      WebSocket upgrade (a stateless JSON endpoint cannot hold a stream, so `leg.stream` and
      every `http.upgrade` entry are never `mcp: true`);
    - the two narrow writes `ticket.hold` (`{hold: true}` only) and `leg.stop` (destructive)
      *(2026-10-18, R-BTN-154: `ticket.expedite` withdrawn from MCP, and a hold only added)*.

    `npm run check:actions` fails on any other `mcp: true`. Never reachable over MCP, so,
    whatever an owner lists:
    - an administrator's action (R-BTN-57: the administrator's key stays out of every agent's
      reach);
    - a machine protocol (the runner's, the sync's, a courier's or a probe's): a session
      inside a leg must not talk to Baton (R-BTN-106);
    - any action that adds, grants, mints, registers or revokes a key, an owner, a token, a
      courier, a check-runner or a sync key — MCP keys included;
    - any write of an R-BTN-66 setting or bar, which hold the limits owners keep against
      agents.
  - **The MCP key.** An MCP caller presents a bearer **MCP key**, an API key of the kind `mcp`
    (R-BTN-117).
    - **Minting.** An owner mints one through its own action, `owner.mcp-key.create`, whose
      `callers` are exactly `[owner]` — no dashboard session or administrator mints one, so
      every key has a minting owner key to die with, and `check:actions` fails otherwise:
      `baton owner mcp-key create <repository> --name <name> [--actions read | <id>,…]
      [--ttl <days>]`, which is `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/mcp-keys`. `--name` is unique in
      the repository. It returns the key once, as `bmcp_` followed by 32 random bytes in
      base32; the prefix is for secret scanning. Baton stores its hash.
    - **What Baton stores.** One `mcp_keys` row (§4): the repository, the name, the key's hash,
      the minting owner key's fingerprint, the action ids resolved at minting, the expiry, the
      last use and any revocation. "The kind `mcp`" names this table, not a `credentials.kind`
      value; `credentials` keeps its fingerprint-keyed rows. `read` means the
      allowlisted `read` ids that exist at minting, so a later release never widens a key.
      `leg.stop`, the destructive one, is included only when listed by id. An id outside the
      allowlist, or outside the owner's own actions, is refused at minting.
    - **Lifetime.** At most 90 days (default 30); 7 days with no call end it. The last use is
      written at most once a minute per key.
    - **Death and refusal.** The key dies when its minting owner key is removed or revoked.
      While the repository's owners have `api_keys: false` it is refused, as every API key is
      (R-BTN-117), and it works again when the setting returns to `true`, if it has not
      expired. Its owners revoke it with `owner.mcp-key.revoke` (`POST
      /v1/owner/{repository}/mcp-keys/{name}/revoke`, `confirm: true`). It is listed with
      the repository's credentials, with its minter.
  - **How it authorizes.** `authorize` treats an `mcp` principal as its minting owner, on its
    one repository, narrowed to its stored ids — an id that has since lost `mcp: true` is
    refused. The action is recorded as `mcp:<name>`, minted by that owner, in history and in
    release messages. An MCP key is accepted only on `POST /v1/mcp`; every REST route answers
    it `unauthenticated`.
  - **The endpoint.** `POST /v1/mcp` speaks MCP's streamable HTTP transport, statelessly, in
    JSON (no server-sent stream):
    - Revisions: the ones the build lists in `MCP_VERSIONS` (at least `2025-06-18`), as
      `initialize` negotiates. `initialize` needs no `MCP-Protocol-Version` header. On any
      other request an absent header means `2025-03-26`, as the transport says, and a revision
      not in `MCP_VERSIONS`, given or assumed, is `400`.
    - Methods: `initialize`; `notifications/initialized`, and any other notification,
      answered `202`; `ping`; `tools/list`; `tools/call`. Any other method is JSON-RPC
      `-32601`, and a batch array is `-32600`.
    - Sessions: Baton keeps none and issues no `Mcp-Session-Id`.
    - `GET /v1/mcp` is `405`.
    - A missing or unknown key is `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
    - A request carrying an `Origin` header other than Baton's own is refused `403`, as the
      transport requires against DNS rebinding.
  - **Tools.**
    - `tools/list` returns the key's stored ids that still carry `mcp: true`. The name is
      the id with `.` as `_` (`leg_stop`): ids have no `_`, so names never collide.
      `inputSchema` is the entry's `input`, and the annotations come from `effect`
      (`readOnlyHint` for `read`, `destructiveHint` for `destructive`).
    - `tools/call` runs the same core function as the route. Its result carries the output
      as `structuredContent` and as text, through the `plain` renderer (R-BTN-112).
    - A refusal is a tool error with the route's refusal code. A tool the key does not hold,
      an unknown tool, and a target outside the key's repository all answer the same
      `forbidden`, so MCP is no existence oracle (P7).
  - **`confirm` over MCP is a schema check, not a human gate.** The agent that passes it is the
    agent a hostile ticket might steer. The safeguard is the owner's choice at minting —
    `leg.stop` only by explicit id — together with the key's narrow list.
  - **Content is data.** Ticket titles, decision text and readings come from git and from
    workers. They are returned as JSON values and rendered text, never as instructions, and
    the tool descriptions say so (P8). An agent reads a leg's log through `leg.runs`, which
    returns the run's pointers and live state, never the log's bytes: Baton holds none
    (R-BTN-128).
  - **Bounds.**
    - **Rate.** At most 60 calls per key in any 60 seconds, counted in the repository's
      object, in memory. A restart empties the counter, which is the one burst it allows. A
      call over the limit is refused `rate-limited`, with `retry_after_s`.
    - **Pages.** A tool whose output is a list takes an optional `cursor` input and returns
      `next_cursor`. The cursor is opaque, bound by an HMAC under `CursorKey` (R-BTN-55) to
      the key, the action and the input, and refused under any other.
    - **Size.** A page is at most 256 KB; a single item larger than that is refused
      `too-large`.

### 2m.7a The wire, the settings and the interfaces

§11's existing rows gain these fields; §11 also lists §2m's new routes.

| Row | Gains |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/runner/heartbeat` | `isolation: 'attached' \| 'process' \| 'session'`; `session_url?` for the running leg (R-BTN-107, R-BTN-113) |
| `POST /v1/runner/advance`, `POST /v1/runner/end` | `session_url?` for the leg finished; each output as the envelope `{name, schema, uri?, digest?, value?}` (R-BTN-108); refusals `not-eligible` with rules `chain`, `isolation`, `person`, `entry` |
| `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/couriers` | `{public_key, delivers: ['forge-check']}` beside `{public_key, asks}` (R-BTN-115) |
| `POST /v1/courier/notices/claim` | `?delivers=forge-check`; the notice `{notice_id, kind: 'forge-check', repository, origin, forge_repo_id, sha, name, conclusion, summary, seq, issued_at, kid, signature}` (R-BTN-114, R-BTN-136) |
| `POST /v1/courier/notices/{id}` | `check_id` when marking a `forge-check` notice `sent` |
| `PUT /v1/owner/{repository}/settings` | `api_keys`, `required_independence`, `checks`; `retry` as `{default, ceiling: {max_attempts, max_attempts_s, in_claim, max_interval_s, max_refreshes, max_blocked, initial_s}, never_retry}` (R-BTN-117, R-BTN-106, R-BTN-114, R-BTN-122, R-BTN-123) |
| `POST /v1/runner/end` (released) | `error: {type, message?}` (R-BTN-122); the reason `blocked` with `prerequisite: {kind, ref}`, for a resource `reading: {instance, available: false, until?, valid_for?, detail?}`, for a ticket or decision `commit`; refusal `invalid-prerequisite` (R-BTN-126) |
| `POST /v1/runner/heartbeat` (leg logs) | `leg_logs: [{claim, leg, run, repo, path, pushed_at, bytes}]` (R-BTN-128) |
| `GET /v1/repositories/{repository}/tickets/{ticket}/legs/{leg}/runs` *(new)* | each run's claim, worker, times, session link, log and transcript pointers; for an owner key of the repository or an administrator key (R-BTN-128) |
| `GET /v1/actions` *(new)* | the caller's own registry entries, with their `input` schemas (R-BTN-129) |
| `POST /v1/mcp` *(new)* | MCP's streamable HTTP transport: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, for an MCP key (R-BTN-130) |
| `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/mcp-keys` *(new)*, `…/mcp-keys/{name}/revoke` *(new)* | an owner mints `{name, actions, ttl}`, returning the key once, or revokes it with `confirm: true` (R-BTN-130) |
| The destructive routes (R-BTN-129) | `confirm: true` in the body: `…/overrides/{ticket}` with `cancel`, `…/tickets/{ticket}/release`, `/v1/ui/claims/{id}/reap`, `…/owners` removals, `…/grants` and `…/couriers` revocations, the check-runner, token and MCP-key revocations, `/v1/admin/keys/{fingerprint}/revoke`, a repository's retirement |
| `GET /v1/stream?claim=<id>` *(new)* | the CLI's viewer upgrade, signed by an owner or administrator key (R-BTN-128) |
| `PUT /v1/owner/{repository}/settings` (logs) | `leg_logs: true` (R-BTN-128; default `false`) |
| `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/tickets/{ticket}/release` *(new)* | `{reason: 'requested', confirm: true}`: **Stop leg** from the CLI, an owner's release message (R-BTN-119, R-BTN-127) |
| `POST /v1/runner/advance`, `POST /v1/runner/end` (leg logs) | `leg_logs` pointers pending, as on the heartbeat (R-BTN-128) |
| `POST /v1/runner/claim`, `POST /v1/runner/advance` (replies) | `leg_logs: {repo}` while the repository's owners have it on (R-BTN-128) |
| local channel | `baton leg release --blocked --kind <kind> --ref <ref> [--instance <i>] [--until <RFC 3339>] [--valid-for <s>] [--detail <json>] [--commit <sha>]` (R-BTN-126) |
| board post: each ticket's `decisions` | `severity?` (R-BTN-125) |
| `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/couriers` (again) | `severities?` beside `asks` (R-BTN-125) |
| `POST /v1/courier/notices/claim` (decision notices) | `decision.severity` (R-BTN-125) |
| `POST /v1/runner/heartbeat` (worker couriers) | `couriers: [{repository, asks, severities?}]` (R-BTN-125) |
| `POST /v1/runner/activities` | the kind `context-handoff`, with both sessions' links (R-BTN-123) |
| `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/check-runners`, `…/{fingerprint}/revoke` *(new)* | an owner registers or revokes a check-runner key (R-BTN-114) |
| `PUT /v1/admin/settings` *(new)* | an administrator sets `link_hosts` and `session_hosts`, kept in a new single-row `instance_settings` table (R-BTN-112, R-BTN-113) |
| **Stop leg** (the dashboard) | the existing `POST /v1/ui/messages` with `{kind: 'release', payload: {ticket_id, reason: 'requested'}}` (§9) — no new route; *(2026-10-17, R-BTN-127)* the CLI's `baton leg stop` uses `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/tickets/{ticket}/release` |
| `baton owner key create --api` | `POST /v1/owner/{repository}/grants` with `{name, api_key: true, capabilities, max_tier?}`, returning `{api_key}` once (R-BTN-117) |

**R-BTN-55's interface table gains** `CursorKey` (Cloudflare: the `BATON_CURSOR_KEY` secret; local: `--cursor-key <file>`; R-BTN-130), `Stream` (Cloudflare: a Durable Object per claim on the
hibernation API, named under its tenant's id, R-BTN-135; local: an in-process fan-out) and `SigningKey` (Cloudflare: the
`BATON_SIGNING_KEY` secret; local: a key file), so S-BTN-68 and S-BTN-70 run on both hosts.
**§4 gains** `instance_settings` (`link_hosts`, `session_hosts`), `check_runners`
(credential, repository), `claim_legs.session_url`, `closed_tickets.final_station` and
`final_path`, schemas keyed `(repository_id, id, version)`, `leg_attempts` (repository,
ticket, leg, `attempts`, `first_attempt_at`, `retry_after`, `last_error_type`; R-BTN-122),
`claims.error_type` (the message is not stored, R-BTN-33), `ticket_blocks.kind` `retry`,
`couriers.severities`, `notices` carrying `severity`, `ticket_blocks.provisional` (the commit a provisional row waits for) and `ticket_blocks.found` (`before-start` or `during-run`), `leg_needs.source` (`posted` or `end`), `added_at` and `found_at`, `claims.blocked_kind` and `blocked_ref` with an index on (ticket, leg, ended_at), the hold reason `blocked-exhausted` (R-BTN-126), `leg_logs` (claim, leg, run, repo, path, pushed_at, bytes; R-BTN-128), `repositories.leg_logs`, `claim_legs.leg_logs_repo`, `mcp_keys` (id, repository, name, hash, minter fingerprint, action ids, expires_at, last_used_at, revoked_at; R-BTN-130), and the owner settings above.

### 2m.7 What core gains

R-BTN-50's table gains, all generic: the action registry and `authorize` (R-BTN-129), the `mcp` credential kind (R-BTN-130); a leg run's log pointers (R-BTN-128); the `blocked` end with its prerequisite, and a leg edge's state (R-BTN-126); an output's envelope and schema id; a schema's id,
version, digest and base; a station's `entry`; a leg's `no_chain_from`, `isolation`, `kind:
person`, `asks`, `stream` and `spawns`; a check course's `checks` map; a worker's `isolation`;
a leg run's `session_url`; the `watch` and `unwatch` rings; the `forge-check` notice; the
`forge-courier` credential kind; registration tokens and API-key credentials; and the
discrepancy subs `output-invalid` and `check-mismatch`; a leg's `requires` (`tickets`,
`capabilities`, `resources`), a ticket's posted `depends_at`, `ticket` blocks per leg with
`at` or `reached`, and a course's `capability_types` and `capability_roles` (§2m.6); the check-runner key role; and
the **Needs you** entry `prerequisite-cycle` (§2m.6); a course's `error_types`, a leg's
`retry`, `max_ready_s` and `max_attempts_s`, the `retry` block kind, an end's `error`, and
attempt counts per ticket and leg (§2m.6a); a leg's `max_context` and `max_refreshes`, the
`context-handoff` activity, a ticket prerequisite's `done`, and a decision's `severity` (§2m.6b).

### 2m.8 Scenarios and gates

- **New scenarios** (§13a):

  | Scenario | Setup | Outcome |
  |---|---|---|
  | S-BTN-62 a session reports to its runner | a runner runs `implement` by handing it to an agent session; the session sends `done` with a `reached` that is not an outcome, then a valid move without the station's required output, then a valid move | the first two are answered on the channel with their reasons and nothing reaches Baton; the third is closed, advanced and recorded; the state view the session was given holds no worker secret or nonce |
  | S-BTN-63 no review by its author's key | a claim runs `implement` and reaches `pr-open`; its runner tries to advance into `review`, which names `implement` in `no_chain_from`; it suspends, then claims the ticket again under the same key; the course file drops the list while the owners' `required_independence` names it | the advance and the second claim are refused, rule `chain`; a runner under another key takes `review`; with the list dropped from git the owner setting still refuses the first key |
  | S-BTN-64 isolation floors | a leg requires `isolation: session`; an `attached`, a `process` and a `session` worker ask for recommendations | only the `session` worker is offered it; the others' claims and advances into it are refused, rule `isolation` |
  | S-BTN-65 refinement | a course schema refines `std:forge.change@1` but drops `head_sha` from `required`; a second keeps it; a leg reports a value missing `url` against the second | `baton course test` reports the first, naming `required`; the value fails both its schema and the base, and the leg ends `released:cannot-finish:contract-output` |
  | S-BTN-66 entry requirements | `reviewed` requires `findings` of `roadmap:findings@2`; a leg reaches it with no `findings`, then with an inline value, then with a pointer the sync finds invalid | the first advance is refused, rule `entry`; the second is accepted and validated in full; the third is accepted, then posted invalid, logged `output-invalid`, and its consumer waits on `input-missing` |
  | S-BTN-67 a person's leg | a ticket's queued leg is `approve`, `kind: person`, `asks: owner`; a worker asks for it; the owner answers in git; on a second ticket the answer the sync posts lacks `option` | the worker is not offered it and its claim is refused, rule `person`; the decision is open with its notices; the next snapshot posts the path through `approve` with a `std:decision@1` output, and the decision closes; the second ticket's arrival is logged `output-invalid` and listed under **Needs you** |
  | S-BTN-68 the merge check | a check-runner's check ticket ends at `passed`; the forge courier posts its notice; a push supersedes the head; a token posts a status context of the same name; the check App posts a success Baton never issued; an agent edits the course file's `checks` to map `failed` to `success`; Baton's signing key is rotated | a signed `success` notice is queued only after the sync confirms the end; the new head gets its own ticket and an `in_progress` notice; the status context does not satisfy the required check; the unissued success is logged `check-mismatch`; the edited `checks` changes nothing, the owners' setting holds; earlier check runs still verify under the retired key |
  | S-BTN-69 registration and API keys | an owner mints a token with `--ttl 30d --max-tier 2`; one session registers an SSH key, another an API key; a third tries `--max-tier 3`; the repository sets `api_keys: false` | both get grants within tier 2; the third is refused; after the setting the API-key worker is refused at its next call, the SSH worker is not; revoking the token revokes both |
  | S-BTN-70 watching a leg | a viewer opens a running leg's stream; the leg prints 200 KB a second; a runner that ignores the limit sends 1 MB a second; a page on another origin, a viewer naming an unknown claim and one naming a `stream: false` leg try to open streams; a second worker opens `/v1/runner/stream` for the first one's claim; the viewer leaves | the runner is rung `watch`, sends its scrollback, then frames with `gap` markers at the rate limit; the stream channel drops what the misbehaving runner sends over the limit; the three refused upgrades all answer `forbidden` and ring nothing; the second worker's upgrade is refused `forbidden` and no frame of its reaches the viewer; 60 seconds after the viewer leaves the runner is rung `unwatch`; Baton's storage and logs hold no frame |
  | S-BTN-71 stopping a leg | a leg runs a process that ignores `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`; the dashboard's **Stop leg** is pressed | the runner sends `SIGINT`, then `SIGTERM` after 10 s, then `SIGKILL` at 25 s; the group is gone within 30 s of the release reaching the runner; it calls `close` and `handoff` and ends `released:requested` with no output reported; no hold is set |
  | S-BTN-72 tickets at stations | a parent's `integrate` requires its children `at: merged` and its own epic `reached: planned`; one child is merged, one is at `review`; the epic has moved on to `building`; a second ticket's leg requires a parent it does not have | `integrate` is blocked by one `ticket` row, the child at `review`, until it merges, then offered; the epic counts (`reached`); the second ticket's prerequisite is unmet, `no-parent`, and listed under **Needs you** |

  | S-BTN-107 the build-app course (R-BTN-131, B-40) | a fresh repository runs `baton repo init`, then `--course build-app`, with one request; the drafting legs' markers land one by one, the owner setting `answer:` after each; `file` adds two children on `create-pr` naming the request as `parent`; they close one at a time; a first verification files a fix child and returns `building`, a second returns `shipped` | the request starts at `requested` with `define` ready; after each draft the next leg waits on `owner` until `answer:` names that draft's stage, an earlier stage's name holding it; at `building` `verify` waits on `children` until the last child closes, again after the fix child is filed, and is ready once it closes; `shipped` has no next leg |
  | S-BTN-106 a ticket's PRs in other repositories (R-BTN-74, R-BTN-96, R-BTN-131; B-29, B-35) | a repository whose ticket names two other repositories in `repos:` — its home gets no PR — syncs against a recorded GitHub; a closed ticket names a third; the review's verdict line lands on one PR; then one PR merges, then the other | the sync reads the home and the two repositories the live ticket names, never the closed ticket's, each owned PR's detail in one GraphQL query for its repository and never over REST; the ticket is `pr-open` from their PRs; the verdict on one PR makes the change `reviewed` with `merge` queued; one merged leaves it there; both merged is `merged` |
  | S-BTN-105 a course from its source, one leg overridden (R-BTN-131, B-33) *(superseded 2026-10-19 by S-BTN-110, §2p: a source at another commit or repository is now read, not refused, and there is no home course file to edit; only the override's half stands)* | a repository runs `baton repo init --override review`: its `create-pr` names `github/<owner>/<name>/<commit>/create-pr` at the CLI's commit, and `legs/review.run.mjs` replaces the review's run; a claim's `review` runs the override at the snapshot; then, one at a time, the course file edited, the source at another commit, the source in another repository, and a `sync.mjs` beside the source | the sync posts the course and places the ticket at `pr-open`; the override runs and the standard `close` writes the verdict line, which moves the ticket to `reviewed` with `fix` queued; each of the four is refused, naming what to do, and nothing is posted until the last is undone |
  | S-BTN-104 the standard courses (R-BTN-131, B-28) | a fresh repository runs `baton repo init`, then `--course bug-report` and `--course decision`, with a ticket on each; the bug report's legs commit closing markers to `.baton/markers.jsonl` (with a marker that is no edge and a malformed line among them); the decision's owner sets `answer:`; a second repository runs on `draft-ticket` alone with no forge facts and no token | each ticket starts at its course's start with its start leg queued; the bug report follows its markers to `closed`, the marker that is no edge and the malformed line changing nothing, its queued leg the marker's `next`; `carry-out` waits on `owner` until `answer:` is set, then is ready; the second repository syncs and places its ticket at `requested` |

- **New gates** (Must-establish, §16):

  | New invariant | Proven by (gate test) |
  |---|---|
  | A session's move reaches Baton only after the runner has checked its station, its next leg, its outputs and the station's entry; a session is handed no worker secret, and in `session` mode can reach none | G-BTN-89 (S-BTN-62, -78) |
  | A claim or an advance into a leg is refused when the credential ran, on that ticket, a leg the target names in `no_chain_from` or the owners' `required_independence`, or the worker's declared isolation is not the leg's floor, or the leg is a person's | G-BTN-90 (S-BTN-63, -64, -67) |
  | A value is valid only against its schema and every base; the test kit reports every refinement it cannot prove; one validator module serves server, CLI, sync and kit | G-BTN-91 (S-BTN-65) |
  | An arrival at a station without its entry outputs is refused; an inline value is validated in full; a pointer the sync posts invalid is never resolved as an input | G-BTN-92 (S-BTN-66) |
  | A `success` merge check is queued only after a sync confirms the end and its entry, with the owners' conclusions; every check notice is signed with a named key; a check run Baton did not issue is logged; a forge courier is never a machine key and its notices never go to the pool | G-BTN-93 (S-BTN-68) |
  | A token-registered credential never exceeds the token's scope and dies with it; an API key is refused on a repository with `api_keys: false` and in any role but worker or personal courier *(2026-10-17, §2m: or an MCP key on `POST /v1/mcp`, R-BTN-130, G-BTN-121)* | G-BTN-94 (S-BTN-69) |
  | Leg output is relayed only from the claim's holder, only while an authorized same-origin viewer is watching, within Baton's own size and rate bounds, never for a `stream: false` leg, and is never written to storage, logs or exports | G-BTN-95 (S-BTN-70) |
  | Cancel and a release message stop the leg's process group within 30 seconds of the release reaching the runner, and report no output of the stopped leg | G-BTN-96 (S-BTN-71) |
  | A leg is offered only when its station, its ticket prerequisites (`at`, `reached` or `done`, a withdrawn ticket skipped only where the entry says so), its and its ticket's capabilities, its resources and every decision on it or its ticket hold; each unmet one is a block row on that leg | G-BTN-97 (S-BTN-72, -74) |
  | A course file's capabilities are of declared types with matching values or built-in; a runner declares a checked capability only while its check passes; a grant's `<type>:*` covers the type | G-BTN-98 (S-BTN-73) |
  | A bounded run claims only named legs, starts at most `n` per claim and none after `until` | G-BTN-99 (S-BTN-75) |
  | Every renderer escapes or text-sets every value, and links only to the repository's `web_base` or `link_hosts` | G-BTN-100 (S-BTN-76) |
  | A `session_url` is kept only on an allowlisted host, `https`, no userinfo, at most 512 characters | G-BTN-101 (S-BTN-77) |
  | A schema posted with a changed digest, outside the subset, with an unsupported pattern, in a `$ref` cycle, or under a `std:` id or another course's prefix is refused; schemas are keyed per repository | G-BTN-102 (S-BTN-79) |
  | Only a check-runner key claims a check ticket; the conclusions come from the owners' setting; an unsent `forge-check` is listed after 15 minutes | G-BTN-103 (S-BTN-68, -81) |
  | A prerequisite cycle keeps its blocks and is listed; a withdrawn ticket meets no prerequisite; `reached` on a closed ticket reads its final path | G-BTN-104 (S-BTN-82) |
  | A leg in backoff is a `retry` block until its `retry_after`: refused at claim and advance, absent from recommendations, shown by `baton leg why`; the schedule is the policy's, jittered ±10%, counted per ticket and leg | G-BTN-105 (S-BTN-83) |
  | A course-declared non-retryable type holds at once; an untyped error is `transient`; in-claim retries count neither as runs nor as attempts | G-BTN-106 (S-BTN-84, -85) |
  | The policy in force is, field by field, the stricter of the course's and the owners' bounds on every quota-spending field (`max_attempts`, `max_attempts_s`, `in_claim`, `max_interval_s`, `max_refreshes`, `initial_s`, `coefficient` ≥ 1); the floor binds on built-in types; `max_attempts_s` stops retries once spent | G-BTN-107 (S-BTN-86, -87) |
  | A leg past its `max_context` is refreshed under the same claim, at most `max_refreshes` times, counting neither a run nor an attempt, then suspended | G-BTN-108 (S-BTN-88) |
  | The `epic` course's `integrate` is queued only when no withdrawal is unanswered by a `replan`, and starts only when every child not withdrawn closed `done`; `children` selects closed children; `skip_withdrawn` alone lets a withdrawn ticket out of an entry | G-BTN-109 (S-BTN-89) |
  | Notices carry their decision's severity; a courier receives only the severities it registered, and one that gains a severity gets the open decisions of it; an `(asks, severity)` no personal channel takes is listed; reminders and lists follow severity | G-BTN-110 (S-BTN-90) |
  | A `resource` blocked end stores its reading and an `end` need, then writes that ticket's row against R-BTN-76's counts, in one transaction; a worker with another usable instance is still offered the leg; dropping the need deletes its row; no attempt, run or backoff is spent and the ticket stays at its station | G-BTN-111 (S-BTN-91) |
  | A `capability` blocked end removes the capability from the runner's declared set in its transaction; a row is written only when no live runner holds it | G-BTN-112 (S-BTN-92) |
  | A `ticket` or `decision` blocked end writes only a provisional row that refuses a claim into its leg but does not count toward `blocked_since` and raises no notice or event, confirmed or replaced only by a snapshot containing its commit and dropped after an hour otherwise | G-BTN-113 (S-BTN-93) |
  | An invalid prerequisite — including a reading for an instance that does not serve `ref` or that the worker may not report on — is recorded by Baton as a counted `cannot-finish:transient` end in the refusing call; a reading that fails only its envelope, bounds or rate limit is dropped and the end stands; an error naming a valid prerequisite is never retried, in the claim or after | G-BTN-114 (S-BTN-93, -94) |
  | Blocked ends per (ticket, leg) past the owners' `max_blocked` in 24 hours hold the ticket and raise `baton:retries`; a legacy `provider-exhausted` is recorded as a `blocked` end with a reading of the one used instance serving the leg's needs only when none is in force (never shortening one), and with none or several is recorded without a reading and counted toward `max_blocked` unless the worker's own unavailable reading of a serving instance is in force | G-BTN-115 (S-BTN-95) |
  | Every view draws each leg as an edge with a state shown in colour and text, `found` `during-run` for a resource row whose need carries a `blocked` end's stamp (whoever wrote the row) and `before-start` for a row that predates the claim, and draws no station the course file does not name | G-BTN-116 (S-BTN-96) |
  | Every command is `baton <noun> <verb>` and signs as the one role its route needs; each old top-level name does nothing but name its replacement; an ambiguous ticket id names its matches; the channel verbs act only inside a leg's session | G-BTN-117 (S-BTN-97) |
  | A `process`-mode leg run's output is archived only when the owners set `leg_logs: true`, only to the repository's `transcript_repos` at the claim's own path, never for a `stream: false` leg, with the closed credential set masked on the byte stream before framing and at most 50 MB per run; a failed push never delays the end; Baton stores only valid pointers bound to their claim; `baton leg log` reads the archive from git with the user's credentials, strips every escape and control on every path it prints, and exits 1 when it cannot read | G-BTN-118 (S-BTN-98) |
  | The CLI's stream upgrade is accepted only for an owner key of the claim's repository or an administrator key, under R-BTN-118's rules, and closed when that key is revoked; the CLI joins archive and stream on `seq`, printing no frame twice | G-BTN-119 (S-BTN-99) |
  | Every route, CLI command, dashboard action and MCP tool is a registry entry, authorized by the one `authorize` call; `GET /v1/actions` shows a caller only its own actions; every listed destructive action needs `confirm` on every surface; `check:actions` fails on any unregistered surface, bad id or out-of-allowlist `mcp` flag | G-BTN-120 (S-BTN-100, -102) |
  | An MCP key reaches only its stored, still-allowlisted ids on its one repository, accepted only on `POST /v1/mcp`; it never reaches an administrator action, a machine protocol, a credential or owner change, or an R-BTN-66 write; out-of-scope, unlisted and unknown targets answer alike; the transport, rate and page rules hold | G-BTN-121 (S-BTN-101) |
  | An MCP key's ids are fixed at minting; it dies with its expiry, 7 idle days, its minting owner key or its revocation, and is refused while `api_keys` is `false` | G-BTN-122 (S-BTN-103) |

  | A ticket's PRs in every repository it names are read under one budget, the owned PRs' detail batched over GraphQL, matched by repository and number, and read together as one change: a verdict on any of them stands for all, and it is merged when every one is | G-BTN-125 (S-BTN-106) |
  | A course named by its source runs the source's graph exactly — the sync refuses a course file that differs, a source at another commit or repository, and a `sync.mjs` beside it — and a repository's `<leg>.run.mjs` replaces that leg's run, read at the snapshot, never its close | G-BTN-124 (S-BTN-105) *(superseded 2026-10-19 by G-BTN-129, §2p, except that an override replaces only a leg's run, never its close)* |
  | A `build-app` leg never starts on a document the owner has not approved — each waits on `owner` until `answer:` names the stage it builds on — and `verify` never starts while a child is open | G-BTN-126 (S-BTN-107) |

## 2n. One primitive per kind of prerequisite *(amendment 2026-10-19, owner direction; proposal; built by B-41)*

*(Owner, 2026-10-19: "The course description vocabulary has both requires and blocked on. Can
you please verify that we do not have a set of overlapping primitives for legacy reasons in the
course schema?" — then: "file the ticket with the spec amendment". The audit, the same day,
found five ways to say a ticket waits for other tickets, three to say it waits for a person and
two to say it needs `human-operator`, most of them older than R-BTN-120 and kept for it.)*

What follows is the whole of the change. R-BTN-120 made a leg's prerequisites one list of kinds;
this amendment makes each kind have **one** way in, retires the others through a transition
window, and states the pairs that look alike and are not overlaps. **Scope, stated:** no new
prerequisite kind, block kind, route or principal; core still reads no course meaning (R-BTN-50);
git stays the truth (R-BTN-39).

- **R-BTN-132 (one primitive per kind of prerequisite).** *(Amends R-BTN-69, R-BTN-74, R-BTN-75,
  R-BTN-86, R-BTN-116, R-BTN-120, R-BTN-131 and §7.2 rule 6.)*
  - **What overlapped.** Before this rule:

    | kind | ways in | what core read |
    |---|---|---|
    | other tickets | `depends_on`, `blocked_by` and `parent` posted per ticket; a station function's `waiting_on: dependencies` or `children`; a leg's `requires.tickets` and the posted `depends_at` (R-BTN-120) | `blocked_by` alone, as whole-ticket `ticket` blocks; `depends_on` stored unread, turned by the standard courses into a label on the start leg only |
    | a person | a posted `decision` (R-BTN-78); a `kind: person` leg (R-BTN-116); a station function's `waiting_on: owner` over the ticket's `answer:` (R-BTN-131's interim) | decisions, and the label as an opaque wait |
    | `human-operator` | a capability in the ticket's `requires`; `operator_only`, from the `OP` tag, checked by its own rule 6 | rule 6 only: the capability was kept out of `ticket_requires` |

  - **Other tickets: a leg's `requires.tickets`, and `depends_at` for what varies per ticket.**
    These are the only ticket prerequisites core reads once the window closes. The ticket
    source keeps the authority R-BTN-75 gave it — it posts only the dependencies it counts
    open, so a dependency docs counts finished (superseded, archived before Baton) is simply
    not posted — but it posts them as `depends_at` entries, which Baton evaluates against the
    stations and paths it stores, never as a pre-judged `blocked_by` list.
    - **`depends_on`** stays a word of the default markdown source, not of the board post: the
      source translates each id to `{ticket, done: true, leg: <the course's start_leg>}`, which
      keeps today's behaviour exactly (the standard courses wait only the start leg on it). A
      file that wants another leg, or a station, writes `depends_at` itself.
    - **`blocked_by`** is retired from the board post. During the window core reads each posted
      id as `depends_at: {ticket, done: true}` with no `leg`, a whole-ticket `ticket` row as
      today, so a source that has not moved behaves as before.
  - **Children: `parent` is the link, never a block.** R-BTN-86's fan-in moves from the ticket
    source onto the legs that fan in. The default source stops adding open children to their
    parent's `blocked_by`; a leg that must wait for its children says so,
    `requires.tickets: [{select: "children", done: true}]` (with `skip_withdrawn` where the
    course replaces withdrawn children, as `epic` does). The parent's other legs are no longer
    blocked by an open child, so a parent may work beside its children (`epic`'s `replan`; an
    interactive leg's children, B-34). A course that wants the old whole-parent behaviour puts
    the entry on every leg leaving the station.
    - **The window before the sync stays closed.** A `spawned` list still writes provisional
      `ticket` rows in the end's transaction (R-BTN-86), now on each leg leaving the station
      reached whose `requires.tickets` selects `children`, and on the whole ticket when no leg
      does; they are replaced by the first accepted snapshot observed after the end, as before.
      Without them a leg whose earlier children have all closed `done` — a second verification
      after a fix child is spawned — would hold before the snapshot posts the new child.
  - **A person: a person's leg or a decision.** A wait for an answer is a `kind: person` leg
    (R-BTN-116), whose output the next station may require (R-BTN-109); a wait that needs no
    typed answer is a posted decision (R-BTN-78). A station function no longer emits
    `waiting_on: owner`. The standard courses move when person legs are built (B-7), each as
    a new course version that replays its in-flight tickets (R-BTN-48) — `decision`'s
    `carry-out`, `create-pr`'s `adjudicate` answered `owner`, and `build-app`'s four approvals
    each gain a person's leg whose path git shows by the answer the interim already reads.
  - **`human-operator` is a capability like any other.** The sync stores it in
    `ticket_requires` and rule 4 checks it; `operator_only` and the `OP` tag become source
    vocabulary, translated by the default source and docs' `tickets.mjs` to `human-operator` in
    the ticket's `requires`. **Rule 6** keeps only what is particular to it: `human-operator` is
    granted by an administrator alone (R-BTN-58).
  - **`waiting_on` is for what no kind covers.** A station function's label stays for waits
    only the course can see — an author's push (`review-pr`), CI (`short_waits`), any effect
    the sync reads back from the forge — and Baton keeps showing it under `other` (R-BTN-120).
    It may not be `dependencies`, `children` or `owner`, nor `policy`, which core writes for a
    required bar: after the window the snapshot validator refuses them, naming the ticket.
  - **Not overlaps, stated.** The ticket's `requires` clause and a leg's
    `requires.capabilities` join (R-BTN-120: the clause binds every leg, the list one). The
    `needs` the sync posts and a leg's `requires.resources` join too: one is computed at each
    sync, the other fixed in the course file. A station's `entry` (R-BTN-109) checks what a leg
    produced on arriving, not whether a leg may start. None of these is changed; the posted
    field keeps its name `requires` (a wire rename across every ticket source would cost more
    than the two meanings do, and each is read only beside its owner).
  - **The window** (`cross_repo_migration`, dual-read). Phase 0: core builds `depends_at` and
    `requires.tickets` (B-10), and `ticket_requires` takes `human-operator`. Phase 1: core reads
    `blocked_by`, `operator_only` and the reserved labels as above, and logs one
    `deprecated-field` event per repository and field per day. Phase 2: the default source,
    docs' `tickets.mjs` and the standard courses write only the new forms. Phase 3: **Needs
    you** lists each repository whose snapshot still carries an old form. Phase 4, alone and
    last: the board-post validator refuses `blocked_by`, `operator_only` and the reserved
    labels, and a new migration stops storing `tickets.depends_on`, `tickets.blocked_by` and
    `tickets.operator_only`.

  S-BTN-108, G-BTN-127.

  | S-BTN-108 one primitive per prerequisite (R-BTN-132, B-41) | a repository on the default source: a ticket whose `depends_on` names an open ticket; a parent at a station with two legs out, one requiring its children done; a ticket tagged `OP`; then, on a second repository still posting `blocked_by` and `operator_only`, the same tickets | the dependency waits the start leg only, as `ticket@done` on that leg; the parent's other leg is ready while a child is open and the fan-in leg waits until both close, a `spawned` child holding it before the snapshot posts it; the `OP` ticket refuses a worker without a granted `human-operator` by rule 4; the second repository behaves the same and is listed under **Needs you** with `deprecated-field`; after cutover its snapshot is refused naming the field |

  | Must hold | Gate |
  |---|---|
  | A ticket prerequisite reaches core only as a leg's `requires.tickets` or a posted `depends_at`; an open child blocks only the legs that select children (and, until the snapshot, the provisional rows of its `spawned` end); `human-operator` is checked by rule 4 alone; and a station function's label is never `dependencies`, `children`, `owner` or `policy` | G-BTN-127 (S-BTN-108) |

## 2o. A leg runs in a checkout of its commit *(amendment 2026-10-19, owner direction; proposal; built by B-42)*

*(Owner, 2026-10-19: "a user's legs should be typescript, mjs or regular non-module js. Node
should perform module resolution (dependencies should be declared in the repo's package.json)"
— then: "please make the spec amendment, this is important". Until now the runner extracted
each `legs/<leg>.mjs` from the snapshot into a scratch directory (§6.13), so a leg could be
`.mjs` only, and it could import only Node built-ins: from the scratch directory, Node finds
no `package.json` and no `node_modules`.)* *(Revised 2026-10-19 after an adversarial review of
three reviewers, round 1 on PR 57; the owner chose that dependencies are installed from the
course directory or `.baton/`, never the repository root, so a push that leaves the lockfile
alone costs no install.)*

What follows is the whole of the change. A leg's script stops being a loose file and becomes a
file **in a checkout**: a sparse, read-only git worktree at the commit the claim names, with the
dependencies its lockfile declares installed, so Node resolves its imports and decides its
module format as it does for any file in a repository. **Scope, stated:** no new route, wire
field, end reason or principal; core gains one built-in capability type (`runner`, below) and
nothing else; Baton still runs no repository code (R-BTN-102); what a leg runs is still read
from git at a commit, never from a working tree (R-BTN-34, B-33).

- **R-BTN-133 (a leg runs in a checkout of its commit).** *(Amends R-BTN-5, R-BTN-34, R-BTN-51,
  R-BTN-65, R-BTN-72, R-BTN-105, R-BTN-119, R-BTN-121, R-BTN-131 and §2d's test kit. A sourced
  course's trees are R-BTN-134's.)*
  - **The commit is the default branch's** — R-BTN-143's check, which this rule does not
    restate: against the registered branch, in the runner's own ref, one fetch, `off-branch`
    when it fails, and the held-rewrite cache. It runs before any of this rule's preparation, so
    an off-branch `snapshot_sha` is never checked out and its lockfile never installed; without
    it, every runner would install an unmerged branch's dependencies as well as run its leg
    scripts. *(Revised 2026-10-19 on merging §10.7: this bullet first defined its own check,
    ending `stale-board`; R-BTN-143 is the one check, and R-BTN-147 replaces an unfounded head,
    so no loop guard is needed here.)*
  - **The leg trees.** The runner makes sparse, detached worktrees, in non-cone mode
    (`git sparse-checkout set --no-cone /.baton/` or `/<course path>/`, so not even the root's
    files are checked out): the home repository at
    `snapshot_sha` with only `.baton/` checked out — `ctx.snapshot.tree` — and, for a sourced
    course, the source repository at its commit with only the course directory checked out
    (R-BTN-134). The **course directory** — `.baton/courses/<course>/` in the home tree, or the
    source's path in its tree, named by `ctx.course.dir` — is the module root of the leg's
    script; the home tree holds the overrides (R-BTN-131). Sparse trees cost what `.baton/` and
    one course directory cost, not a whole checkout, and no `package.json` above them is checked out for Node or npm to find; and because the trees
    sit inside the home checkout's git directory, below its working tree, the runner writes
    `{"private": true}` as `<git dir>/baton/package.json` (refusing to start if it cannot), so the
    nearest `package.json` of any tree file is within the tree or that stop file, never the
    working tree's. A tree is keyed by (repository, commit, checked-out path) and
    lives at `<git dir>/baton/trees/<provider>/<namespace>/<repository>/<commit>-<the first 12
    hex of SHA-256 of the path>`, its stamp `<that path>.ready` beside it — under the home
    checkout's git directory, so the one runner that holds the home checkout (R-BTN-131's lock)
    is the one writer of its trees. It is reused by a later claim at the same key; the runner
    keeps the three it used last per repository and removes the others when a claim ends
    (restoring their write bits, then `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune`).
    Every git command the runner runs — on a tree, the home checkout or a cache clone — passes
    `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false`, so no hook or monitor the home
    checkout's config names, which agents can write, ever runs.
  - **A tree is verified on every use.** On reuse, the runner checks the stamp, re-checks the
    commit's ancestry against the branch head it has just fetched (never a stored ref), and
    checks that the tree is clean: `git status --porcelain --ignored=matching
    --untracked-files=all` lists nothing but the install roots' `node_modules` links, each
    pointing at its digest's directory. A tree that fails any check is removed and made again.
    A tree holding a symbolic link — other than those links, which are the runner's — whose
    target resolves outside the tree, or a submodule entry, ends the claim
    `released:cannot-finish:spec`, naming it.
  - **Dependencies: the course directory's, then `.baton/`'s.** A tree's **install roots** are
    the course directory and, in the home tree, `.baton/`: each that has a `package.json`
    declaring any `dependencies` is installed; one that declares none (a `package.json` that only
    sets `type`) needs no lockfile and installs nothing, and never hides the other. The
    repository root is never an install root: a repository whose legs need a library declares it
    in `.baton/package.json` or the course's own. Each install root needs a
    `package-lock.json` or `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, and must not declare `workspaces`. The runner
    runs `npm ci --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund` (npm ships with Node, so a runner needs no
    other package manager); a `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `yarn.lock` instead ends
    `released:cannot-finish:spec` naming the file, and so does a `package.json` with
    dependencies and no lockfile, and a `file:` dependency on a directory (one on a tarball,
    which the lockfile hashes, is allowed).
    - **The dependency cache.** An install is made once per **digest** — the SHA-256 of the
      lockfile, the install root's `package.json`, `process.versions.modules`,
      `process.platform`, `process.arch` and npm's version, joined by newlines in that order, each
      file's bytes as its SHA-256 — in `<git dir>/baton/deps/<digest>/`,
      which the tree's install root links as its `node_modules`; so a push that leaves the
      lockfile alone installs nothing, and a Node upgrade or another machine installs afresh.
      Once installed, the digest's directory has its write bits cleared and a stamp, `<digest>.ready`
      beside it, written holding the SHA-256 of its file list and contents, re-checked before each
      leg; on a mismatch the directory is removed and installed again. A digest no kept tree
      links is removed with the last tree that did; removing a tree never changes a digest's
      bits.
    - **Failures.** An install whose npm error says the lockfile and `package.json` disagree
      (`EUSAGE`), or that names a package the lockfile lacks, ends
      `released:cannot-finish:spec`; a full disk (`ENOSPC`) ends `cannot-finish:capability`;
      every other failure — the registry, the network — ends `transient`, retried under
      R-BTN-122's policy.
  - **Preparation is fenced and bounded.** R-BTN-143's fetch, the source fetch (R-BTN-134),
    `git worktree add`, the install and the write-bit walk are the claim's **preparation**,
    each run as an asynchronous child in its own process group — never a synchronous call, so
    the sidecar keeps heartbeating (§6.3) — under R-BTN-26's fence. A lost lease kills the
    running step's group at once; Cancel and a release message stop it by R-BTN-119's sequence
    (`SIGINT`, `SIGTERM` after 10 seconds, `SIGKILL` after 25). No leg has run, so the claim
    ends with no `close` and no `handoff`: its station and resume record are where the next
    claimant starts, as after a lost lease (R-BTN-24). Preparation is bounded by `baton runner
    start --prepare-timeout <duration>` (default 15 minutes), past which the step's group is
    killed and the claim ends `released:cannot-finish:transient`. A tree without its stamp is
    unfinished, and is removed, never used.
  - **Languages.** A leg's script is `legs/<leg>.<ext>` and an override `legs/<leg>.run.<ext>`
    (R-BTN-131), `<ext>` one of `mjs`, `js`, `cjs`, `mts`, `ts`, `cts`. The format is Node's
    decision, by its own rules from the tree, including its syntax detection for a `.js` or
    `.ts` file that no `package.json` `type` covers. TypeScript runs by Node's own type
    stripping, so the runner requires Node 22.18 or later and refuses to start on an older one,
    naming the version. That means **erasable syntax only** — no `enum`, no namespace with
    values, no parameter properties, no `import =` or `export =` — relative imports that name
    their file's extension, type-only imports written `import type`, and no `tsconfig` `paths`;
    a `.cts` file is CommonJS, so it imports by `require`; type checking is the repository's CI's
    job, never the runner's. A dependency under `node_modules` must ship JavaScript (Node strips
    no types there). Two scripts for one leg (`implement.ts` beside `implement.mjs`) fail the
    test kit, and a runner that meets them ends `released:cannot-finish:spec`.
  - **The wrapper: resolution held to the trees.** Every call of a script — `run`, and also
    `close` and `handoff`, which until now ran inside the runner's own process — goes through
    the CLI's wrapper, `legProcess.mjs`, spawned detached in its own process group, with
    `ctx.checkout` as its working directory (a leg works in the checkout; the tree is not
    writable), and with `NODE_OPTIONS` and `NODE_PATH` removed from its environment. So no tree
    code is ever loaded into the long-lived runner that holds the worker secret — `rank.mjs`
    (R-BTN-98) included, which runs through the same wrapper. The wrapper is called as `node
    legProcess.mjs <call> <script> <ctx.json> <out.json>`, `<call>` one of `run`, `close` (its
    `ctx.json` carries the validated `result` beside the context), `handoff`, and, for
    R-BTN-134's whole-commit tree, `tickets`, `stations` and `rank`; `out.json` receives `{ok,
    result | ref | url, error?, aborted?}`. `close` and `handoff` are bounded at 2 minutes
    each, then killed as a failure of that call, retried as R-BTN-72 says. The wrapper registers
    a resolve hook (`module.registerHooks`) that answers `@immediately-run/baton/leg` with the
    running CLI's own module, whatever a tree installs, and refuses any other resolution outside
    the claim's trees, their linked digests and the paths R-BTN-134's `imports` allows (no
    `~/node_modules`, no `node_modules` above `<git dir>/baton/`, no global folders), naming the
    specifier.
    The runner tells a `LegError` by a brand the module sets (`Symbol.for('baton.LegError')`),
    never by `instanceof`. The wrapper takes `run`, `handoff` and `close` as named exports, else
    from the default export, so a CommonJS script's `module.exports` works as an ES module's
    exports do.
    - **The leg module**, one list: `@immediately-run/baton/leg` exports `LegError`,
      `writeMarker` (R-BTN-131's marker append with its rebase-and-retry), `commentOnPr`
      (through the fact adapter's forge, R-BTN-96), `yieldContext` (the channel's `yield`,
      R-BTN-123), `nextFire`, `writeSuccessor` and `NOT_BEFORE_HORIZON_DAYS` (R-BTN-89), and
      `CLI_VERSION`. It carries no course meaning.
  - **The tree is read-only to legs.** Once a tree's preparation finishes, the runner clears
    the write bits of every file and directory in it (a walk that never follows a link) and
    writes the stamp. A tree is shared by every claim at its key, so a leg that edited it would
    change what a later leg runs — the property B-33 holds for instructions (a branch under
    review cannot rewrite its reviewer), held for scripts too. Like R-BTN-106's isolation, this
    binds a cooperating leg, not a hostile one: a leg runs as the runner's user and could
    restore the bits, which the clean check on reuse catches. A leg that needs a cache writes
    under its scratch directory or `$TMPDIR`.
  - **Trust, stated.** A leg's script and every install script of its dependencies run with the
    worker's full rights, as leg scripts always have (§6.13 **Trust**); the lockfile pins exact
    versions and their integrity hashes, at a commit of the default branch. An older commit
    of the default branch passes too, with its older lockfile — R-BTN-143's **Older
    default-branch code, stated**.
  - **Old runners are kept off by a capability.** Core gains a second built-in capability type,
    **`runner`**, beside `human-operator` (R-BTN-121): `runner:<feature>` names a feature of the
    runner itself. Only the runner declares it — from its own code, never from its
    configuration — and rule 4 treats it as granted to every worker key, so it needs no grant
    and stays self-reported (R-BTN-60). Its values are the features the CLI defines —
    `leg-trees` today — and the test kit and the sync refuse another, so a misspelled feature is
    caught before it makes a leg unclaimable; a runner refuses to start when its configuration
    names a `runner:` capability; and a course may declare no type named `runner` or
    `human-operator`. This rule's runner declares `runner:leg-trees`; so does a sidecar that
    runs no leg script, such as an interactive session's (R-BTN-72's **Both ways of working
    stay**), since it runs none of the code the feature gates. A course must list
    `runner:leg-trees` in the `requires` (R-BTN-120) of every leg whose script is not `.mjs`,
    imports `@immediately-run/baton/leg`, or whose course directory or `.baton/` declares
    dependencies, and of every leg of a sourced course. The test kit fails a course that does
    not, and so does the sync before it posts, naming the leg — so a third-party source that
    omits it is refused by every home that names it. Baton refuses a claim and an advance into
    such a leg by a worker that does not declare it (rule 4, `not-eligible`), and leaves it out
    of that worker's recommendations. `min_worker_version`
    cannot do this: rule 9 compares it with the course `version` the worker reads from its own
    checkout (R-BTN-65), which an older runner on a pulled checkout already has. A course of
    `.mjs` legs that import only Node built-ins needs no capability and runs the same under
    both runners.
  - **The test kit.** `baton course test <repository root> <course>` (§2d) accepts the same
    extensions, fails two scripts for one leg and a leg missing `runner:leg-trees` where it is
    required, and imports each script and override from the repository root it is given through
    the same wrapper and resolve hook. It installs each install root itself, with the runner's
    command (`--omit=dev`), into a cache of its own run, and resolves only from there — so a leg
    importing a devDependency fails the kit as it would fail a runner — and an import it cannot
    resolve fails it, naming the specifier. The kit runs the PR's code, so its CI job runs on
    `pull_request` with a read-only token, no `id-token` and no `BATON_SOURCE_TOKEN`, never on
    `pull_request_target`; a private source then cannot be fetched, and the kit fails that
    course naming the token, unless the operator opts the job in.

  S-BTN-109, G-BTN-128.

  | S-BTN-109 legs in a checkout of their commit (R-BTN-133, B-42) | a repository whose `.baton/package.json` declares one dependency as a `file:` tarball, with its lockfile; course legs `implement.ts` (importing the dependency), `review.cjs`, `fix.mts`, `merge.mjs`, `adjudicate.cts` and `close-out.js`, each requiring `runner:leg-trees`; the runner started under Node 22.17, refused naming the version, then under 22.18 or later, with injected stop timers; two claims at one commit, a push that leaves the lockfile alone, then one that changes it; then, one at a time: a board posted with a `sha` off the default branch; a lease lost during the install; Cancel during the install; `fix.ts` beside `fix.mjs`; a `yarn.lock`; an import of a package installed only in the user's home; a runner that does not declare `runner:leg-trees` | each leg runs and its result is reported, `close` and `handoff` in the wrapper; the first claim installs once, the second and the push that kept the lockfile reuse the install (the runner's log shows one install per digest), the changed lockfile installs again; the off-branch `sha` is released `off-branch` (R-BTN-143) before any install; the lost lease kills the install's group and writes no hand-off; Cancel stops it within 30 seconds and ends `released:owner-cancel`; the kit fails the two `fix` scripts; the `yarn.lock` ends `released:cannot-finish:spec` naming it; the import from the home is refused naming the specifier; the runner without the capability is not offered the legs and its claim is refused, rule 4 |

  | Must hold | Gate |
  |---|---|
